blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (One customer query per invoice (N+1)) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The loop runs `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1` once per invoice: with the proposal's ~3 000 invoices a month that is ~3 000 sequential round trips (for only ~800 distinct customers), growing linearly with invoice volume on the report finance reads. Collect the distinct `customer_id`s, load them in one call with the existing `db.customers(&ids)` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`), index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>`, and build each label from the map. Keep the current error behavior for an invoice whose customer is missing (return a `DbError` rather than skipping the line).
findings.title: One customer query per invoice (N+1)

findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for every invoice and calls `Regex::new` each time, so the pattern is parsed and compiled ~3 000 times per report, a cost far larger than the match itself and growing with invoice volume. Compile it once — a `static PATTERN: std::sync::LazyLock<Regex>` (or `once_cell::sync::Lazy`), or build it in `monthly_report` before the loop and pass `&Regex` in.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled once per invoice
